finding.claim: Unauthenticated insecure deserialization: attacker-supplied Base64 `state` param is passed directly to Marshal.load, allowing arbitrary object instantiation and remote code execution via Ruby gadget chains.
finding.source: POST /restore form/query parameter `state` (params[:state]), fully attacker-controlled, no authentication required

trace.note: params[:state] is Base64-decoded and passed straight to Marshal.load
Deserialized object is inspected and returned, also triggering methods on the object

finding.guards_checked: No authentication, no signature/HMAC on the payload, no class allowlist, no input size limit; the app has no before filters or middleware. Sinatra's Rack::Protection does not prevent this (CSRF/origin checks do not block direct attacker requests).

verdict.reason: app.rb:5-6 defines an unauthenticated POST /restore that passes Base64.decode64(params[:state]) straight to Marshal.load, with no auth, signature, or allowlist, and app.rb is the only file in the directory so no filters or middleware exist. Line 7 only calls inspect on the result, which is a minor misdescription, but the RCE occurs at the load itself.
